title: The Last Day at the Kiln

collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — ROLE MODELS AND GOOD EXAMPLES, RM-41 to RM-90 (draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Fifty more events continuing your "Role Models and Good Examples — 40 Events". Same shape as yours: a SETUP, choices A-D (a few have three), and two possible outcomes per choice; the game picks one outcome from the chosen choice.

ledger.why: the owner (2026-11-15): the person the event is about is a cast villager shown by name, the role word kept as flavor (the villager need not have that job)

collection.description: An elderly potter announces that they are ready to stop working, and the village must decide how to respond.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (Name1), an elderly potter, announces that they are ready to stop working, and the village must decide how to respond.

choices.label: Ask the Potter to Teach One More Lesson.
Keep the Kiln Ready in Case They Return.
Ask What the Potter Wants Next.

a1.name: Outcome A1
a1.text: The village holds a gathering, and the potter is deeply moved.

a2.name: Outcome A2
a2.text: The potter prefers a quiet farewell, and the village honors that.

b1.name: Outcome B1
b1.text: The potter agrees and shares a technique nobody else knew.

b2.name: Outcome B2
b2.text: The potter declines, saying it is time to rest, and the village respects it.

c1.name: Outcome C1
c1.text: The potter visits occasionally and makes a pot for fun.

c2.name: Outcome C2
c2.text: The potter never returns, and the kiln passes to an apprentice.

d1.name: Outcome D1
d1.text: The potter wants to fish, and the fishers welcome them.

d2.name: Outcome D2
d2.text: The potter wants to simply rest and watch the sea.
